verdict.rationale: Google Drive's own sharing docs cover the core of a data room: folders can be shared with anyone, access set on a folder is inherited by the files inside it, and sharing can be limited so recipients can only open (view) files. The other two elements are not shown as product features: nothing in the evidence documents download, print or copy restrictions, and access visibility appears only as API building blocks (a permissions resource and a sample for auditing sharing info into a spreadsheet), not as a built-in viewer-activity view. missing for 10: download/print/copy restriction controls, built-in access visibility or viewer activity for diligence, link expiration or audit evidence, independent hands-on corroboration of data-room use.

support.subject: As a founder, I can run a lightweight data room — organized shared folders with view-only links, download controls, and access visibility for diligence

citations.quote: When you share from Google Drive, you can control whether people can edit, comment on, or only open the file.
Access you apply to a folder is inherited by all files within it.
You can share the files and folders that you store in Google Drive with anyone.
